cross_component_finding: The code examples on this page are not Python. Both the Ping example ('let services = [couchbase.ServiceType.KeyValue, couchbase.ServiceType.Query]', 'bucket.ping(services, (err, res) => {...})') and the Diagnostics example ('bucket.diagnostics((err, res) => {...})') are fenced as ```javascript``` blocks using Node.js callback-style syntax, and the mock JSON output's embedded 'sdk' string literally reads 'libcouchbase/2.9.5-njs couchnode/2.6.9 (node/10.16.0; ...)' - couchnode is the Node.js SDK, not the Python SDK. This is a concrete content-quality finding, not just a modeling one: the page appears to have been copied from (or never updated from) the Node.js SDK's equivalent health-check documentation and never adapted to Python syntax - no ping()/diagnostics() call shown anywhere uses Python method-call or dict-return conventions. Filed as docs-issues/python-sdk-health-check-leftover-nodejs-sample-output at reconciliation (round 30).
cross_product_finding: Placement difference confirmed by directory listing: Java's SDK docs have health-check.md only under howtos/ (java-sdk/current/howtos/health-check.md exists; there is no concept-docs/health-check.md for Java), treating Health Check as a task/how-to. Python's SDK docs place the identically-named page under concept-docs/ instead (python-sdk/current/concept-docs/health-check.md), treating the same ping()/diagnostics() feature as a concept to be explained rather than a task to be performed - even though this page's actual content (method calls, JSON output, no numbered procedure) reads more like a howto than a concept page. This is a page-type/taxonomy inconsistency between the two SDKs' doc trees for the same feature, independent of the content-quality (wrong-language-code-example) finding above. Folded into docs-issues/java-python-sdk-rbac-page-structure-inconsistency at reconciliation (round 30) as a second confirmed instance of the same cross-product IA pattern.
